title: Minimum Distance Excluding One Maximum Weighted Edge
summary: Given a positive integer n and a 2D integer array edges, where each edge is defined as [ui, vi, wi], find the minimum cost of a path from node 0 to node n-1, excluding the edge with the maximum weight in the path.
statement: Given a positive integer n and a 2D integer array edges, where each edge is defined as [ui, vi, wi], find the minimum cost of a path from node 0 to node n-1, excluding the edge with the maximum weight in the path. If multiple edges have the same maximum weight, only the first one is excluded from the cost calculation.
constraints: 2≤n≤50,000; edges form a connected simple undirected graph with positive weights.
A path costs its edge sum minus one occurrence of its maximum edge.
Return the minimum possible cost from node zero to node n-1.
hints: For any fixed path, excluding its maximum edge is equivalent to choosing one edge to traverse for free optimally.
Each edge either adds its weight or, if unused, consumes the one free traversal at zero cost.
The minimum over all paths and free-edge choices always chooses a maximum edge on its selected path.
editorial: The minimum over all paths and free-edge choices always chooses a maximum edge on its selected path.

tests.explanation: The only path sums to twenty; excluding one maximum-weight edge leaves thirteen.
Taking the direct edge and excluding it gives cost zero.
